title: BNCI 2015-009 AMUSE (Auditory Multi-class Spatial ERP) dataset
description: The BNCI 2015-009 AMUSE dataset comprises EEG recordings from 21 healthy subjects performing an auditory oddball task using spatial hearing cues for brain-computer interface applications. Participants discriminated target and non-target stimuli presented from five spatially distributed speakers with varying inter-stimulus intervals. The dataset includes preprocessed EEG data acquired at 250 Hz and downsampled to 100 Hz from 60 channels, with documented best-subject performance metrics of 100% accuracy and 25.2 bits/min information transfer rate.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a Brain Products 128-channel amplifier at 250 Hz sampling rate from 60 channels with Ag/AgCl electrodes in 10-20 montage, referenced to nose. Auditory stimuli consisted of 40ms complex sounds from bandpass-filtered white noise with tone overlay, presented from five speakers with 45-degree spacing. Three experimental conditions were tested: C300 (300ms inter-stimulus interval), C175 (175ms ISI), and C300s (300ms ISI, single speaker). Preprocessing included analog bandpass filtering (0.1-250 Hz), notch filtering at 50 Hz, downsampling to 100 Hz, and threshold-based artifact rejection (>70 µV on ocular channels).
